quiz_flutter_basics.title: Flutter Basics Quiz
quiz_flutter_basics.description: Test your knowledge of Flutter fundamentals including widgets, state management, and layouts

questions.questionText: What is Flutter?
options: A UI framework for building cross-platform apps
questions.explanation: Flutter is Google's UI toolkit for building beautiful, natively compiled applications for mobile, web, and desktop from a single codebase.

questions.questionText: Which programming language is primarily used with Flutter?
questions.explanation: Flutter uses Dart as its programming language, which was also developed by Google.

questions.questionText: What does 'StatelessWidget' mean in Flutter?
options: A widget that has no state and never changes
A widget that manages database state
questions.explanation: StatelessWidget is immutable and its properties can't change—all values are final.

questions.questionText: Which widget is used for scrollable lists in Flutter?
questions.explanation: ListView is the primary widget for creating scrollable lists in Flutter.

questions.questionText: What command is used to create a new Flutter project?
questions.explanation: The 'flutter create' command is used to create a new Flutter project with all necessary files and folders.

quiz_dart_advanced.title: Advanced Dart Programming
quiz_dart_advanced.description: Deep dive into Dart language features including async programming, streams, and null safety

questions.questionText: What keyword is used to define an asynchronous function in Dart?
questions.explanation: The 'async' keyword is used to mark a function as asynchronous in Dart.

questions.questionText: What does the '??' operator do in Dart?
options: Null-aware operator that returns the right operand if the left is null
questions.explanation: The '??' operator returns the right-hand operand if the left-hand operand is null, otherwise it returns the left-hand operand.

questions.questionText: Which collection in Dart does NOT allow duplicate values?
questions.explanation: Set is an unordered collection of unique items in Dart.

questions.questionText: What is a Stream in Dart?
questions.explanation: A Stream provides a sequence of asynchronous events. It's like an asynchronous Iterable.

questions.questionText: What does 'late' keyword indicate in Dart?
options: The variable will be initialized later before first use
questions.explanation: The 'late' modifier means the variable will be initialized later, but before it's used for the first time.

questions.questionText: How do you create a constant list in Dart?
questions.explanation: Using 'const' creates a compile-time constant list that cannot be modified.

challenge_algorithm_basics.title: Algorithm Problem Solving
challenge_algorithm_basics.description: Solve algorithmic challenges covering arrays, strings, and basic data structures

questions.questionText: What is the time complexity of binary search in a sorted array?
questions.explanation: Binary search has O(log n) time complexity as it divides the search space in half with each iteration.

questions.questionText: Which data structure uses LIFO (Last In First Out) principle?
questions.explanation: Stack follows the LIFO principle where the last element added is the first one to be removed.

questions.questionText: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort?
questions.explanation: QuickSort has a worst-case time complexity of O(n²) when the pivot is poorly chosen.

questions.questionText: In a hash table, what happens when two keys hash to the same index?
options: Collision - resolved using techniques like chaining
questions.explanation: Hash collisions are resolved using techniques like chaining (linked lists) or open addressing.

questions.questionText: Which algorithm is best for finding the shortest path in a weighted graph?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm is specifically designed to find the shortest path in weighted graphs with non-negative weights.

challenge_data_structures.title: Data Structures Challenge
challenge_data_structures.description: Master fundamental data structures: arrays, linked lists, trees, and graphs

questions.questionText: What is the main advantage of a linked list over an array?
questions.explanation: Linked lists allow dynamic memory allocation and efficient insertion/deletion operations.

questions.questionText: In a binary search tree, what property must be maintained?
options: All nodes must have exactly two children
Left subtree values < node value < right subtree values
All leaves must be at the same level
questions.explanation: BST property: left subtree contains only nodes with values less than the parent, right subtree contains only nodes with values greater.

questions.questionText: Which traversal method visits nodes in the order: Left-Root-Right?
questions.explanation: Inorder traversal visits left subtree, then root, then right subtree.

questions.questionText: What is the height of a complete binary tree with n nodes?
questions.explanation: A complete binary tree has height O(log n) as it's fully filled except possibly the last level.

questions.questionText: Which data structure is best for implementing undo functionality?
questions.explanation: Stack is ideal for undo operations as it maintains a LIFO order of actions.

questions.questionText: What is a circular queue?
options: A queue that never gets full
A queue where rear connects back to front
questions.explanation: A circular queue treats the array as circular, connecting the rear back to the front to reuse space.

exam_mobile_dev_comprehensive.title: Mobile Development Comprehensive Exam
exam_mobile_dev_comprehensive.description: Complete assessment covering Flutter, Dart, UI/UX design, and app architecture

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the BuildContext in Flutter?
options: To provide location of a widget in the widget tree
questions.explanation: BuildContext represents the location of a widget in the widget tree and is used to access inherited widgets.

questions.questionText: Which state management solution is built into Flutter?
questions.explanation: setState() is the built-in method for state management in StatefulWidgets.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the pubspec.yaml file?
questions.explanation: pubspec.yaml defines project dependencies, assets, fonts, and other project metadata.

questions.questionText: Which widget is used for navigation in Flutter?
questions.explanation: Navigator manages a stack of Route objects and provides methods for managing the stack.

questions.questionText: What does 'hot reload' do in Flutter?
options: Injects updated source code files into running app
questions.explanation: Hot reload injects updated source code into the running Dart VM, preserving app state.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between MainAxisAlignment and CrossAxisAlignment?
options: MainAxis is horizontal, CrossAxis is vertical
MainAxis is the primary direction, CrossAxis is perpendicular
MainAxis is for Row, CrossAxis is for Column
questions.explanation: MainAxis aligns children along the main direction (horizontal for Row, vertical for Column), CrossAxis aligns perpendicular to it.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of keys in Flutter?
options: Uniquely identify widgets and preserve state
questions.explanation: Keys help Flutter identify widgets uniquely and preserve their state when the widget tree changes.

questions.questionText: Which method is called when a StatefulWidget is removed from the tree?
questions.explanation: dispose() is called when a StatefulWidget is permanently removed from the tree and should clean up resources.

questions.questionText: What is a Future in Dart?
options: An object representing a potential value or error available in the future
questions.explanation: A Future represents a computation that doesn't complete immediately and will have a value or error available in the future.

questions.questionText: Which layout widget allows children to overflow into a scrollable view?
questions.explanation: SingleChildScrollView makes its child scrollable when the child's size exceeds the viewport.

exam_programming_fundamentals.title: Programming Fundamentals Exam
exam_programming_fundamentals.description: Test your understanding of core programming concepts, OOP, and software design principles

questions.questionText: What is encapsulation in OOP?
options: Bundling data and methods that operate on that data within a class
questions.explanation: Encapsulation is bundling data (attributes) and methods (functions) within a class and controlling access to them.

questions.questionText: What does polymorphism allow in programming?
options: Objects of different types to be treated uniformly
questions.explanation: Polymorphism allows objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common parent class.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between '==' and 'equals()' in most OOP languages?
questions.explanation: == typically compares object references while equals() compares object values/content.

questions.questionText: What is a constructor?
options: A special method called when creating an object
questions.explanation: A constructor is a special method automatically called when an object is created to initialize it.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of interfaces in OOP?
options: Define a contract that classes must implement
questions.explanation: Interfaces define a contract specifying methods that implementing classes must provide.

questions.questionText: What does 'DRY' principle stand for?
questions.explanation: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) encourages reducing code duplication and promoting reusability.

questions.questionText: What is recursion?
questions.explanation: Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a problem by breaking it into smaller subproblems.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of exception handling?
options: Manage and respond to runtime errors gracefully
questions.explanation: Exception handling allows programs to catch and handle errors gracefully instead of crashing.
